## Theoretical and empirical estimands {#what-is-your-estimand}

```{r}
#| label: lundberg-pipeline
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3
# Lundberg et al. (2021) three steps as boxes-and-arrows (ggplot, editable).
steps <- tibble::tibble(
  x = c(1, 2, 3),
  lab = c("Theoretical\nestimand",
          "Empirical\nestimand",
          "Estimation\nstrategy"),
  sub = c("unit quantity +\ntarget population",
          "identification\nassumptions (DAG)",
          "where the R\ncode enters")
)
ggplot2::ggplot(steps, ggplot2::aes(x, 1)) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile(width = 0.8, height = 0.7, fill = ncl_blue) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = lab), colour = "white", fontface = "bold",
            size = 5.2, vjust = -0.3) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = sub), colour = "white", size = 3.6, vjust = 2.0) +
  ggplot2::annotate("segment", x = 1.42, xend = 1.58, y = 1, yend = 1,
           arrow = ggplot2::arrow(length = ggplot2::unit(0.18, "cm")), linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::annotate("segment", x = 2.42, xend = 2.58, y = 1, yend = 1,
           arrow = ggplot2::arrow(length = ggplot2::unit(0.18, "cm")), linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.5, 3.5)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_void()
```

::: {.none}
- The theoretical estimand is stated **outside** any model – before R opens
:::

::: {.src}
@LundbergEtAl2021WhatYourEstimand.
:::

::: notes
Our five analysts and the twenty-nine red-card teams were all handed a question in words, and none of them was told exactly which quantity would answer it. Lundberg and colleagues call that quantity the estimand, and the title of their paper asks for it directly: "What is your estimand?" They split the answer into three steps. First, the theoretical estimand: a unit-specific quantity and a target population, stated in plain words, before any model exists. Second, the empirical estimand, which is what in the observable data corresponds to that quantity – and making that link forces your identification assumptions into the open, which is the job of the causal graph. Only third comes estimation, where R finally opens. When they audited a full year of papers in a top sociology journal, the unit quantity was clearly stated in five out of thirty-two. By their standard, every quantitative study must be able to answer that question before R opens.
:::
